Rashi on Nedarim 14b:1:1.hebrew: הנודר בתורה - שאוכל לך, לא אמר כלום:
Rashi on Nedarim 14b:1:1.english: One who takes a vow by the Torah - [Saying, "By the Torah] that I will eat of yours," he has not said anything.

Rashi on Nedarim 14b:3:1.english: If a Torah scroll is placed on the ground - and he said, "By what is written in it."

Rashi on Nedarim 14b:3:2.hebrew: דעתיה אגוילי - דכשנדר, לא נדר אלא בגוילין שכתוב בהן התורה, דכיון שהיה רואה אותה מונחת על הארץ, סבר: הואיל ומונחת על הארץ, ודאי אין כתוב בה, ולא נדר אלא בגוילין, ולא אמר כלום. אבל אי אמר "בה ובמה שכתוב בתוכה", אפילו אי מחתא אארעא, מוכחא מילתא דודאי שבועה גמורה עשה ודבריו קיימין, אע"ג דמחתא אארעא, דלהכי אמר "בה ובמה שכתוב בה":
Rashi on Nedarim 14b:3:2.english: His mind is on the parchment - For when he vowed, he vowed only by the parchment on which the Torah is written; for since he saw it lying on the ground, he reasoned: since it is lying on the ground, certainly [nothing] is written in it, and he vowed only by the parchment, and he has said nothing [of legal effect]. However, if he said, "By it and by what is written inside it," even if it is lying on the ground, the matter is evident that he certainly made a complete oath and his words stand, even though it is lying on the ground, for that is why he said, "By it and by what is written in it."

Rashi on Nedarim 14b:3:3.hebrew: אבל אי מנקיט ליה בידיה, אפילו אמר "במה שכתוב בה" — דבריו קיימין, ובהכי מיירי הא דקתני "במה שכתוב בה דבריו קיימין". דכיון דמנקיט ליה בידיה בכבוד, ורואה ויודע מה שבתוכה, כי אמר "במה שכתוב בה" דבריו קיימין, דשבועה גמורה חשיבא, <abbr title="וכל שכן">וכ"ש</abbr> כי אמר "בה ובמה שכתוב בה":
Rashi on Nedarim 14b:3:3.english: However, if he is holding it in his hand, even if he said, "By what is written in it," his words stand; and it is of this [case] that it teaches, "'By what is written in it,' his words stand." For since he is holding it in his hand with honor, and sees and knows what is inside it, when he says, "By what is written in it," his words stand, for it is considered a full-fledged oath — and all the more so when he says, "By it and by what is written in it."

Rashi on Nedarim 14b:5:1.hebrew: תרוייהו מיירי בדנקיט לה בידיה, ואהכי תנא "בה" ו"במה שכתוב בה", דהא <abbr title="קא משמע לן">קמ"ל</abbr> דכיון דנקיט לה בידיה — דיודע שהיא כתובה — אי אמר "בה" גרידא, כמאן דאמר "במה שכתוב בה" דמי, ודבריו קיימין:
Rashi on Nedarim 14b:5:1.english: Both [clauses] refer to where he is holding it in his hand, and that is why [the baraita] taught "by it" and "by what is written in it" — for this is what it teaches us: since he is holding it in his hand — for he knows that it is written [inside] — if he said merely "by it," it is as if he said "by what is written in it," and his words stand.

Rashi on Nedarim 14b:6:1.hebrew: קונם שאני ישן שאני מהלך - האומר: יאסר עלי כקרבן אם אני ישן או אני מהלך. והכי גרסינן: גבי נדר "בל יחל", וגבי שבועה "אסור", משום דהאי "לא יחל" דנדר מוקי לה בגמרא דמדרבנן הוא, ודשבועה הוי איסור דאורייתא:
Rashi on Nedarim 14b:6:1.english: Konam that I sleep, that I walk - [This refers to] one who says, "May it be forbidden to me like an offering if I sleep or [if] I walk." And thus we read [the text]: regarding a vow, [we read] "he shall not profane," and regarding an oath, [we read] "it is forbidden," because [regarding] this "he shall not profane" of a vow, the Gemara establishes that it is [a prohibition] by Rabbinic law, whereas that of an oath is a Torah prohibition.

Rashi on Nedarim 14b:7:1.hebrew: קונם עיני בשינה היום אם אני אישן למחר - מה שאני ישן היום יהא עלי בקונם על מנת אם אישן למחר, דאם ישן הוא למחר לוקה על מה שישן אתמול:
Rashi on Nedarim 14b:7:1.english: Konam [be] my eyes in sleep today if I sleep tomorrow - That which I sleep today shall be [forbidden] upon me as a konam on condition that I sleep tomorrow, for if he sleeps tomorrow, he receives lashes for what he slept yesterday.

Rashi on Nedarim 14b:7:2.hebrew: אל ישן היום - דשמא יישן מיד למחר ולא מיקיים תנאיה, ונמצא עובר בבל יחל על מה שישן אתמול:
Rashi on Nedarim 14b:7:2.english: He may not sleep today - For perhaps he will sleep right away tomorrow and his condition will not be fulfilled, and it will turn out that he has transgressed "he shall not profane [his word]" for what he slept yesterday.

Rashi on Nedarim 14b:7:3.hebrew: ורב נחמן אומר יישן היום ולא חיישי' שמא יישן למחר - דלמחר מיזהיר זהיר שלא יישן, כדי שלא ילקה על מה שישן אתמול:
Rashi on Nedarim 14b:7:3.english: And Rav Nachman says: He may sleep today, and we are not concerned that he will perhaps sleep tomorrow - For tomorrow he will surely be careful not to sleep, so that he will not be lashed for having slept yesterday.

Tosafot on Nedarim 14b:3:1.hebrew: הא דמחתא אארעא - והכי דייקינן: סיפא דבעינן תרתי — "בה ובמה שכתוב בה", אבל "מה שכתוב בה" לחוד אמרי' דעתיה אגוילין, וה"ק: "במה שכתוב בה" דהיא הקלף; אבל כשאמר "בה ובמה שכתוב בה", ע"כ מדייתר לשונו שמע מינה דדעתיה אאזכרות שבה. ורישא דנקיט ליה בידיה, הילכך כשאמר "במה שכתוב בה" לחוד דעתיה אאזכרות; אבל "בה" לחוד, לעולם דעתו אגוילין, אע"ג דנקט ליה בידיה. איבעית אימא: רישא מחתא אארעא, והא קמ"ל דמחתא אארעא ואמר "במה שכתוב בה" לחודיה מהני. וה"ג: סיפא דנקיט ליה בידיה, והא [קמ"ל] אע"ג דלא אמר אלא "בה", כמ"ד "שכתוב בה" דמי; והא דקתני סיפא "בה ובמה שכתוב בה", ה"ק סיפא: זימנין ד"בה" לחודה מהני כמה שכתוב בה, והיינו היכא דנקיט ליה בידיה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 14b:3:1.english: This [case] is where it is placed on the ground - And thus we infer: [in] the latter clause, where we require two [expressions] — "by it and by what is written in it," whereas [if he said] "what is written in it" alone we say his thoughts are concerning the parchment, and this is what he means: "by [that upon] which it is written," which is the parchment; however, when he said "by it and by what is written in it," perforce, from the fact that he added extra words to his expression, we learn from it that his thoughts are concerning the mentions [of God's name] that are in it. And the first clause is where he is holding it in his hand; therefore, when he said "by what is written in it" alone, his thoughts are concerning the mentions [of God's name]; however, [if he said] "by it" alone, his thoughts are always concerning the parchment, even though he is holding it in his hand. Alternatively, you can say: the first clause is [where] it is placed on the ground, and this is what it teaches us: that [even when] it is placed on the ground and he said "by what is written in it" alone, it is effective. And thus we read: the latter clause is where he is holding it in his hand, and this is [what it teaches us]: even though he only said "by it," it is as if he said "[by] what is written in it"; and as for that which the latter clause teaches, "by it and by what is written in it," this is what the latter clause means: sometimes "by it" alone is effective just like "by what is written in it," and that is where he is holding it in his hand.

Tosafot on Nedarim 14b:7:1.hebrew: איתמר קונם עיני בשינה היום - ושינה הוא שם דבר בלשון הש"ס, כמו שינה בלשון פסוק:
Tosafot on Nedarim 14b:7:1.english: It was stated: "[Sleeping is] konam for my eyes today" - And sheinah [sleep] is a noun in the language of the Talmud, just like sheinah in the language of Scripture.

Tosafot on Nedarim 14b:7:2.hebrew: רב נחמן אמר ישן ואין חוששין שמא ישן למחר - מפרש טעמיה בגיטין (ד' פד.), דאי בעי מבריז נפשיה בסילוא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 14b:7:2.english: Rav Naḥman said: He may sleep, and we are not concerned lest he sleep tomorrow - [The Gemara] explains his reason in Gittin (84a): that if he wishes, he can prick himself with a thorn [to stay awake].
